name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a 4px solid focus ring in color #005fcc to every interactive element that can receive keyboard focus. This keeps the ring visible on any background and meets WCAG 2.2 AA for 3:1 contrast against both light and dark surfaces. The trade-off is a slight visual bump in crowded UIs, but it’s the fastest way to guarantee keyboard users can always see where they are.

name: Reader
text: The 4px solid focus ring may not be enough on semi-transparent or textured backgrounds, where the ring's color could still blend in, causing accessibility issues. A better alternative would be to use a high-contrast, multi-state focus indicator that adjusts its appearance based on the background, ensuring visibility in all scenarios. To settle this, we need to test the proposed focus ring with various backgrounds and user agents to see if it meets the desired 3:1 contrast ratio and is perceptible by all users.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a 4px solid focus ring in color #005fcc with a 2px semi-transparent black (#000000, 30% opacity) outline behind it. This two-layer approach guarantees visibility on any background—light, dark, or textured—while keeping the WCAG 2.2 AA contrast intact. The trade-off is a slightly thicker visual indicator, but it’s the only way to ensure no user misses focus cues.

name: Reader
text: The two-layer focus ring risks creating a muddy halo on patterned or dark backgrounds, where the 30% black outline could make the #005fcc ring harder to distinguish. A safer fix is a single, high-contrast ring (e.g., white or black) with a 3:1 contrast ratio against *any* background—settle it by testing on 10 live screens with varying textures.
